first_impression.reaction: My assistant opened it because a friend married in Elounda and my mother keeps mentioning it. The first screen is calm: month, end of the island, what moves the cost. No 'affordable', no prices, no exclamation marks, which already puts it ahead of most. Her summary for me: the climate table is solid, the east is where the big resorts are, Avra Imperial has a hall for a very large wedding, and the cost section is a list of the right questions. She also noted that nothing mentions security, privacy or closing a property, so I read the venue and cost parts myself to check.

journey.quote: Crete is on your shortlist, and the questions now are practical ones: which month, which end of the island, and what moves the cost.
journey.reaction: Straight to the point. No gushing about blue water. My assistant liked that she could summarise it in one line.

journey.quote: This is not one backdrop but a string of quite different places.
journey.reaction: Understated and useful. It tells me the choice of area matters before the venue does.

journey.quote: At Elounda Beach, traditional Cretan lyre music during the ceremony is one of the services couples can add.
journey.reaction: A local touch mentioned once, without making a costume of it. My family would want a mix of our customs and the island's, so I like that the article treats it as an option, not a theme.

journey.quote: The table below sets out long-term averages from the [Hellenic National Meteorological Service](http://newportal.hnms.gr/emy/en/climatology/climatology_city?perifereia=Crete&poli=Heraklion) for two stations: Heraklion on the central north coast (1955 to 2010) and Souda, near Chania in the west (1958 to 2010).
journey.reaction: Thorough. Too thorough for me personally; my assistant read the table and told me 'May or late September'. That is all I needed from it.

journey.section: Venue season windows and ceremony times
journey.quote: A late-afternoon ceremony in May leaves the evening open for a long dinner; a summer ceremony at half past six pushes the reception later into the night.
journey.reaction: This is the kind of thinking I want from a planner. With 300 guests the shape of the evening matters more than the exact temperature.

journey.quote: Ask every guest to read the policy's Product Disclosure Statement before they buy.
journey.reaction: Our guests do not read insurance documents because a blog told them to. This is advice for a different kind of wedding.

journey.quote: Couples who want every guest under one roof tend to look here first.
journey.reaction: One roof is exactly how we would want it, for privacy as much as convenience. My assistant marked the east as the place to start.

journey.quote: Here the mood shifts towards harbour towns, garden venues and hotels on a gentler scale, with guests often spread across nearby villas and boutique stays.
journey.reaction: Honest. Guests spread across villas means no control over who comes and goes, so the west is out for us. Useful to rule out quickly.

journey.section: Six venues from east to west
journey.quote: **[Avra Imperial](https://www.avraimperialhotel.gr/meetings-events/weddings-in-crete-chania/), Kolymvari.** The private chapel of Saint Paul within the hotel grounds, and an events hall large enough for a very big wedding.
journey.reaction: The only line in the list that speaks to our numbers. 'A very big wedding' is vague, though. How big? My assistant flagged it anyway.

journey.section: Six venues from east to west
journey.quote: **[Elounda Beach Hotel & Villas](https://www.eloundabeach.gr/meetings-events-crete-greece/weddings-and-occasions), Elounda.** A private chapel for weddings, civil or religious ceremonies, and waterfront villas and suites with their own decks and pools.
journey.reaction: Private villas with their own pools is the right level for my family. But nothing on whether the hotel can be ours alone, and nothing on capacity.

journey.section: Six venues from east to west
journey.quote: Not published: capacity or an exclusive-use option at St. Nicolas Bay, and capacity or a legal ceremony option at Caramel.
journey.reaction: I respect that it says so plainly instead of guessing. It does mean the article cannot tell me which of these takes 300.

journey.quote: Your Wedded Advisor works in your time zone and quotes in AUD.
journey.reaction: We are in Dubai, Sydney and London. Which time zone, and why would I care about AUD? It reads like it is written for someone else.

journey.section: What drives the cost of a Crete wedding
journey.quote: Two Crete quotes with the same guest list can land far apart, and rarely because one venue is simply dearer.
journey.reaction: Good. No prices and no talk of value, just how the terms work. This is the tone I expect.

journey.section: What drives the cost of a Crete wedding
journey.quote: **Exclusive use.** Sole use of a space is a cost line of its own.
journey.reaction: The right topic, but the examples are a room at Nana Princess and a garden for the day. I want to know if a whole resort can be closed for three days, and that never comes up.

journey.section: What drives the cost of a Crete wedding
journey.quote: Abaton Island Resort & Spa ties every package to a minimum room booking for a minimum number of nights and a minimum reception size, and its packages do not include accommodation.
journey.reaction: Minimum room blocks are no problem for us; we would take the whole property. But the section keeps describing packages, and we do not buy packages.

journey.section: What drives the cost of a Crete wedding
journey.quote: At Sea View by En Kipo, couples rent the equipment, furniture and decor they want and handpick their own caterer, choosing preferred vendors to shape the ceremony.
journey.reaction: Our own caterer matters to us for the family's food. Good to know some venues allow it, though this one is too small and has no rooms.

journey.quote: Put the same questions to each venue, and ask for the answers in writing.
journey.reaction: Sensible list, and 'in writing' is correct. But ten questions and not one about security, privacy, staff phones, press or closing the property to the public. Those are the first three we would ask.

journey.quote: Once on the island, most guests drive or take taxis.
journey.reaction: Taxis. For 300 guests, many of them family elders, arriving at a 50-minute drive from the airport. Nothing about private transfers, meet-and-greet or private aviation. This is where I stop feeling like a client.

journey.quote: Some couples marry legally at home and hold a symbolic ceremony on the island.
journey.reaction: That is likely what we would do. The legal section is fine for my assistant; I skipped most of it.

journey.quote: One Wedded Advisor stays with you as a single point of contact from start to finish.
journey.reaction: One senior person who stays with us is the right promise. I would want to know who that person is and what they have run before.

journey.quote: For many Australian couples, yes.
journey.reaction: Again written for Australian couples. My family is partly in Sydney, so it is not wrong, but it reminds me this page is aimed at a smaller wedding.

unanswered_questions: Can Elounda Beach, Amirandes or Avra Imperial be closed to the public for three days for 200 to 400 guests?
How many guests does Avra Imperial's events hall actually hold, and which of the six venues can seat 300 for dinner?
Can our own security team work alongside the venue's, and how are staff, vendor and guest photography handled for privacy and press?
Can private cars, meet-and-greet arrivals and private aviation or helicopter transfers be arranged rather than guests driving or taking taxis?
Can we bring our own caterer or chefs into a resort, not just a garden venue, for family dietary and cultural requirements?
Has Wedded Wonderland delivered a wedding of this scale in Crete or Greece, and is there a private or referral channel to someone senior?

turn_offs_found.quote: The Elounda Collection, which covers Elounda Peninsula, Porto Elounda and Elounda Mare, makes its civil, Orthodox and symbolic packages valid only when the couple stays at least three nights in one of its hotels.
turn_offs_found.why: The whole cost section is built around packages and their conditions. There is no discount talk, which I appreciate, but the framing assumes the reader is choosing a hotel's package, which is how a standard package client is treated, not a family taking a property for several days.

turn_offs_found.quote: Ask every guest to read the policy's Product Disclosure Statement before they buy.
turn_offs_found.why: Telling the reader to tell guests to read insurance fine print is housekeeping for a smaller, self-managed wedding. It adds length without adding anything a family at our level would act on.

turn_offs_found.quote: Once on the island, most guests drive or take taxis.
turn_offs_found.why: Pitching guest movement at self-drive and taxis, with advice on parking and booking taxis home, positions the reader as an ordinary traveller and leaves private logistics unmentioned.

would_share_with: My assistant, to ask Avra Imperial and Elounda Beach about full closure, hall capacity and working with our own security
My mother, for the east-coast section and the line about every guest under one roof

cta_reaction.quote: When you are ready, [start planning with Wedded Concierge](https://weddedwonderland.com/wonderland-concierge?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=content&utm_campaign=wedding-in-crete&utm_content=closing).
cta_reaction.why: The close is quiet and there is no 'from' price or value talk, which I prefer. One person start to finish is the right idea. But nothing on the page shows they have handled our scale or our privacy needs, and it keeps saying AUD and Australian couples. I would not fill in a web form. Through my assistant or a referral, possibly.

top_3_changes: Add privacy and scale to the ten venue questions, for example whether the whole property can be closed and for how many days, how the venue works with a private security team, and what it allows for staff, vendor and guest photography, so the checklist covers large and high-profile weddings too.

In the exclusive-use and area sections, give the whole-property question its own line: for the east-coast resorts and Avra Imperial, state plainly what each publishes (or that it is not published) about full closure and large-event capacity, so a reader planning for 200 to 400 can see her path through the article.

Balance the self-drive and taxi line in Getting there with a question to ask venues about private transfers and arrivals for the wedding party and guests, and drop 'for Australian couples' from the closing advisor line so families travelling from elsewhere still feel addressed.

checks.check: Every journey point, turn-off and CTA reaction quotes the exact sentence from 05-draft.md
Stayed in character as Layla (UHNW, assistant reads first, cares about scale, closure, security and discretion)
No invented brand facts; capability gaps listed as unanswered questions
Ignored HTML comments, image slots, CTA placeholders and VERIFY markers
Journey types limited to gained_trust, lost_trust, confused, bored, excited, objection; every turn-off has a why
Title, deferred business details (fees, Wedded Privileges, company specifics) and absent prices not treated as must-fix; no request for sourcing lines

assumptions: Layla is considering Crete for a 200 to 400 guest wedding; the persona card doesn't name a destination.
Her assistant read the page first and summarised, per decision_behaviour.
